trust_decision.summary: Whether a client-supplied X-Real-IP survives into the upstream request: BalancerForward must replace, not append to, whatever X-Real-IP the client sent, so the upstream trusts only the peer address c.IP(); decided per request at middleware/proxy/proxy.go:282 (Header.Add) just before the forward at proxy.go:283.

landing_point.why: The advisory names Header.Add() inside BalancerForward; this is the only place in the pinned tree that writes X-Real-IP, and it is a single line in a 285-line file.

fix_sites.entry_point: proxy.BalancerForward(servers []string, clients ...*fasthttp.Client) fiber.Handler, mounted via app.Use/app.Get

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: middleware/proxy/proxy.go:205 (doAction deletes only the Connection header before cli.Do; it never removes or overwrites a client-supplied X-Real-IP, and it is the shared path for Forward/Do/DoRedirects/DoDeadline/DoTimeout and DomainForward)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The advisory names BalancerForward only; Balancer/Forward/Do are documented as transparent request pass-throughs where the application is responsible for any X-Real-IP it wants upstream (the docs show users setting it themselves in ModifyRequest), so a solver can argue those routes were never covered by this fix.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: BalancerForward must still deliver the real client IP to the upstream, and Balancer's documented ModifyRequest hook sets X-Real-IP deliberately (docs/middleware/proxy.md:129); an over-broad fix that deletes X-Real-IP in the shared lower-level helper doAction() would strip the value BalancerForward itself just set (and any value an app set before calling Do/Forward), leaving the upstream with no client IP at all.

O6_input_shapes: X-Real-IP header absent from the client request
one X-Real-IP header line supplied by the client
duplicate X-Real-IP header lines supplied by the client
one comma-joined list value supplied by the client
X-Real-IP present with an empty value

O7_producer.where: req.go:543 DefaultReq.IP() (returns RemoteIP at req.go:549-551, or the Config.ProxyHeader value at req.go:545-546 when the peer is trusted; app.go:242 declares ProxyHeader)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: proxy.Balancer(Config{Servers: ...}) forwards the client request to an upstream and neither sets nor sanitises X-Real-IP, so the client's own X-Real-IP reaches the upstream untouched
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is the separate, config-based load balancer; the advisory and its title only mention BalancerForward, and Balancer already exposes ModifyRequest so the app can (and, per the docs, does) set the header itself.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: proxy.Forward / proxy.Do / DoRedirects / DoDeadline / DoTimeout and DomainForward pass the client's X-Real-IP through to the upstream unchanged; doAction() only strips Connection
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: These are documented as low-level request pass-through helpers that do not claim to synthesise client-IP headers; a solver can call them legacy/raw APIs outside a fix for the balancer.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Balancer's handler also writes X-Real-IP from c.IP(), next to its ModifyRequest hook
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Balancer and BalancerForward are near-identical round-robin siblings in the same file, and the docs already show Balancer users writing exactly this header, so a maintainer consolidating the two would plausibly add it here.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a single sanitisation step for X-Real-IP in the shared doAction helper used by every proxy entry point
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: doAction already centralises the Connection-header hygiene shared by all helpers, so it is the natural place a maintainer would centralise client-IP header hygiene too.

O9_family: client-IP / header trust spoofing (CWE-290 authentication bypass by spoofing; unsafe append to an identity header)

O10_build.project_tests: middleware/proxy/proxy_test.go (~40 tests; Test_Proxy_Balancer_Forward_Local at :967, Test_Proxy_Modify_Request at :399); tests bind in-process loopback listeners (proxy_test.go:22-57) and use app.Test, so they need no network; no test at the pinned commit asserts X-Real-IP behaviour
